name: California Attorney-Client AI Redaction Policy
description:
California-specific strict overlay extending the US baseline. California requires full anonymization — not mere tokenization — before inputting client matter information into external AI systems (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6068(e)(1), CA COPRAC Practical Guidance 2026). Key differences from US baseline: (1) case captions are blocked for human review rather than tokenized, because sending any token to an external AI risks re-identification; (2) contact details are elevated to critical — quasi-identifiers in combination can re-identify a client without names; (3) personal quasi-identifiers (DOB, age, gender) are added as they contribute to re-identification under CA's stricter standard; (4) the 2026 agentic AI guidance prohibits autonomous external transmission of confidential information — this policy enforces the hardest available gate on privilege markers.

Key difference from US baseline: Full anonymization required — case captions are blocked (not tokenized); contact details are critical; personal quasi-identifiers (DOB, age, gender) are included; agentic AI autonomous transmission is explicitly prohibited
Scope: Attorney-client confidentiality for AI tool usage — California strict overlay

effect.message: CA: Case caption flagged for attorney review. California's stricter standard (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 6068(e)(1)) requires full anonymization — tokenizing the caption still transmits identifying information to an external AI system, creating re-identification risk. Under the CA COPRAC 2026 Practical Guidance, a lawyer must not permit autonomous external transmission of confidential client information. Action: attorney review and provider-risk evaluation required before any external AI submission.
